scope: Actual Dynamo transactions and Hono HTTP, including existing SPA create/bulk/flag/account clients, solved-problem projection, durable event and historical-attempt teardown (25 teams, 75 attempts), original-account/region snapshots, partial failure, c091 counter-stripping and consumed terminal events, concurrent completion retries, and interruptions before/after the final child commit, account registration/verification state, concurrent revocation and account-delete/connection-reference fences, retained ExternalId initialization/use markers, installation stop/drain across empty filtered pages, and participant CLI issuance with real team-revocation transactions during STS and during the final sequential connection read, fenced by an atomic condition-only credential-release transaction. Participant STS/SSM/CloudFormation are injected; the revoked response contains no credentials. ExternalId provisioning and STS verification are injected in the Local harness; their SDK contracts, CloudFormation and Step Functions are intercepted in separate unit/synth tests. Not AWS latency or RCU capacity guarantees. Native Cryptography Battle additionally reuses the canonical reducer and current artifact pin, with fixed snapshot chunks and HEAD digest/revision, a single atomic snapshot/score-map-ledger/receipt publication, atomic read authorization for no-op/replay, bounded fenced HEAD admission, real expiry/replacement/revocation/close races, interrupted/lost-response recovery, 48-team transaction bounds, retained final state, and installation drain. The canonical meaningful-tick semigroup counterexample is asserted; time rounding and skipped game ticks are not used.
cleanup: The full run used nine unique synthetic tables; the final focused native run used three additional unique synthetic tables with the same existing schemas. All were deleted, and their loopback-only Java processes stopped. No live AWS calls.

performanceAcceptance.normalScreen: 100 participants / 25 teams, one live projection stream per person; 300 requests across three 5-second cycles, 50ms deterministic offsets. 300 HTTP 200; p50/p95/p99 30/47/59ms.
performanceAcceptance.helpOpen: Two independently phased projection streams per person; 600 requests across three 5-second cycles, 25ms offsets. 600 HTTP 200; p50/p95/p99 37/63/112ms. 12 SDK conflicts recovered internally.
performanceAcceptance.largeState: 796867-byte synthetic snapshot: all 100 intents eventually acknowledged within the unchanged 12-retry bound, 100 exact receipt replays, 3 controlled HTTP 409s, 0 retry exhaustion, 0 unexpected errors, and no remaining admission. Total 10853ms, p95 10450ms. This is eventual completion, not a generic capacity or 5-second latency success.
performanceAcceptance.limitations: Official DynamoDB Local and in-process Hono HTTP; not AWS latency, RCU, cost or production capacity guarantees. Global game mutations remain serial. Frontend in-flight coalescing is validated separately and does not merge independently phased timers.

preservedEarlierFailure.observation: The earlier full run after the 20-second request budget exhausted the unchanged bounded client retry limit during the large synthetic-state burst. Its raw failure is retained; it is not overwritten by the passing rerun.
preservedEarlierFailure.fixtureDiagnosis: That synthetic load used a constant now() while admission expiry is based on wall time. A held claim could therefore remain artificially unexpired. Load now uses advancing Date.now(); the synthetic reducer remains clock-independent. Deterministic stale-clock safety tests remain separate. This fixture defect is not proof that it alone caused every failed retry.
preservedEarlierFailure.remainingCriterion: The corrected canonical simultaneous burst still exceeds 5 seconds.
